title: Evaluate network protocols, routing, and infrastructure design: concept decisions 2
teachingQuestion: For this flow, who receives it, which path/plane carries it, where does protection terminate, and what shared dependency can fail?
focalInsight: Addressing, delivery type, topology, plane separation, and cryptographic endpoints jointly determine actual reachability and failure exposure.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Secure Protocols
nodes.definition: Protocol selection based on layer, endpoints, identity, cryptography, metadata, and operational constraints.
nodes.detail: Protocol selection based on layer, endpoints, identity, cryptography, metadata, and operational constraints.
nodes.decision: Compare IPsec, SSH, TLS, and alternatives against the actual communication use case.
nodes.failureExample: Choosing TLS for router administration without host/admin controls leaves management exposed.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Match protocol layer and endpoints to the threat.

nodes.label: Routing
nodes.definition: Control and forwarding decisions that select packet paths between networks.
nodes.detail: Control and forwarding decisions that select packet paths between networks.
nodes.decision: Protect route administration/authentication, filter intended prefixes, monitor changes, and test convergence/failure.
nodes.failureExample: A forged or misconfigured route diverts traffic around an inspection boundary.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Routing policy determines path; secure its update/control process.

nodes.label: Network Planes
nodes.definition: Data, control, and management functions with different permissions and consequences.
nodes.detail: Data, control, and management functions with different permissions and consequences.
nodes.decision: Isolate and strongly authenticate management/control access while monitoring data-plane policy results.
nodes.failureExample: Compromise of a management plane can rewrite every data-plane rule.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Which plane changes device configuration? Management plane.

nodes.label: Management Plane
nodes.definition: Interfaces and functions used to configure, update, monitor, and administer network systems.
nodes.detail: Interfaces and functions used to configure, update, monitor, and administer network systems.
nodes.decision: Use dedicated/brokered paths, MFA, least privilege, logging, time bounds, and emergency rollback.
nodes.failureExample: A public management interface with shared credentials defeats otherwise secure forwarding.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Management plane needs its own protected path and identity.

nodes.label: Topology
nodes.definition: Arrangement of network paths/nodes that determines reachability and shared failure domains.
nodes.detail: Arrangement of network paths/nodes that determines reachability and shared failure domains.
nodes.decision: Choose redundancy, separation, capacity, and inspection placement from service and threat requirements.
nodes.failureExample: Two links sharing one power source or controller are not independent resilience.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Topology shows both available paths and common-mode failure.

nodes.label: store and forward
nodes.definition: Switching that receives a complete frame before forwarding, allowing full-frame checking/error handling.
nodes.detail: Switching that receives a complete frame before forwarding, allowing full-frame checking/error handling.
nodes.decision: Use where inspection/error tradeoffs justify completion latency.
nodes.failureExample: Assuming it eliminates all malicious traffic mistakes frame integrity for policy security.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Store-and-forward waits for the frame before forwarding.

nodes.label: cut through
nodes.definition: Switching that begins forwarding before full frame receipt to reduce latency.
nodes.detail: Switching that begins forwarding before full frame receipt to reduce latency.
nodes.decision: Use only after accounting for error/inspection tradeoffs and service need.
nodes.failureExample: Cut-through can forward a damaged frame before a later error is known.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Cut-through favors latency; it changes validation timing.

nodes.label: Change Management
nodes.definition: Controlled authorization, implementation, verification, and rollback of network policy/configuration changes.
nodes.detail: Controlled authorization, implementation, verification, and rollback of network policy/configuration changes.
nodes.decision: Link route/policy change to owner, test, approval, monitoring, rollback, and review.
nodes.failureExample: An unreviewed ACL change opens a route with no evidence of intent.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Network change needs evidence before and after deployment.

nodes.label: Incident Response
nodes.definition: Coordinated detection, containment, investigation, recovery, and learning for network security events.
nodes.detail: Coordinated detection, containment, investigation, recovery, and learning for network security events.
nodes.decision: Predefine telemetry, authority, safe isolation, communications, and restoration checks.
nodes.failureExample: Blocking a suspected route without preserving evidence can hinder containment and investigation.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Network response balances containment, evidence, and service recovery.
